answer:
Verdict: no

## Scheduling delays (whole trace, offsets 0–30,687.68 ms)

The sampler was preempted only 5 times, for 0.013 ms total; its longest preemption lasted 0.003 ms. After wake-ups, it queued for a CPU 14,986 times, but the median wait was 0.005 ms and the mean was 0.009 ms. One wait reached 29.597 ms, at offset 15,096.074 ms.

During its 134.585 ms waiting to run, the CPU was idle or handling interrupts for most of the time. Among named tasks, maintenance (TID 629355) held it for 22.0% of that waiting time, uploader (TID 629354) for 13.9%, and sensors (TID 629687) for 1.4%. The analysis does not establish that these tasks were more important; maintenance’s priority is unknown, and uploader had the same normal nice level as the sampler. Confidence in this occupancy breakdown is low.

Interrupt handling on CPU 3 was low: at most 0.025% of the CPU in the measured stretch. Overall, the findings don’t show repeated substantial interruption by a higher-priority task. The sampler’s main time was blocked in `clock_nanosleep`—87.7% of its alive time—rather than delayed from running.
